newsitem.title: LATVIA: Estonian Tallinna Pank eyes Lithuania.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Tallinna Pank eyes Lithuania.

text.p: One of Estonia's leading banks, Tallinna Pank, said it was interested in entering the Lithuanian market in cooperation with new Latvian partner, Saules Bank.
Tallinna Pank late last year bought 20 percent of Saules, which is ranked the eighth largest bank in Latvia.
It became the second Estonian bank after Hansapank to enter the Latvian market in what is a trend for increasing regionalisation of the relatively small Baltic market.
A joint Tallinna Pank/Saules Bank statement quoted Tallinna Pank vice-chairman Targo Raus as saying that Lithuania was a country it was eyeing.

"Targo Raus noted that Tallinna Pank was interested in entering the Lithuanian market and if cooperation with Saules Bank was successful the question of jointly developing activity in this direction could be on the agenda," the banks said.
Both and Latvia and Lithuania have suffered recent bank crises but both countries have made good recoveries.
Raus, at a news conference, declined to specify any plans for Lithuania but Saules Bank board member Yuri Shchetinin said that his bank was actively monitoring the neighbouring market.
"We have good relations there and we are following the Lithuanian banking system," Shchetinin said.
Tallinna Pank bought 780,000 Saules Bank shares at 1.29 lats each to gain its 20 percent stake.
But Raus played down the idea that Tallinna Pank wanted to buy the whole of Saules.
"We have no concrete plans to buy more Saules Bank shares," Raus said.
"For Tallinna Pank, the purchase of Saules Bank shares is a good chance to play a role in what we forecast will be a developing bank sector in Latvia," Raus added.
